title: Multiplication Worksheets: Equal Groups and Facts
intro: Teach multiplication with equal groups before asking your student to recall facts.
html:
Teaching notes for parents and teachers

How to teach it

Make four groups of six counters. Connect the groups to 6 + 6 + 6 + 6 and then to 4 × 6. Rearrange the counters into an array without changing the total.

Example to work through together

Use the model below as you explain the example. Have your student point to the quantities as you discuss them.

Each outlined group represents one bag. Count six crackers in each of the four bags.

6 + 6 + 6 + 6 = 24
4 × 6 = 24

Ask your student

What does each factor tell us about the groups?

If your student needs help

If the student adds 4 and 6, have them point to all four groups. Ask them to count the six counters in each group.

Choosing and using the worksheet

Both factors in these worksheets are whole numbers from 2 to 9, so products range from 4 to 81. This set does not include the zero and one facts or a complete times-table chart. The answer key gives each product in the same order as the questions.
